gloss: to push through; to persist in; to force one's way

definitions.gloss: to push through; to persist in; to insist on
definitions.explanation: To carry something through to the end despite opposition or difficulty, especially one's opinion, will, or way of doing things.

definitions.gloss: to force one's way through; to push through physically
definitions.explanation: To physically push through a barrier, crowd, or obstacle.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}の{意見|いけん}を{押|お}し{通|とお}す。
{彼|かれ}は{最後|さいご}まで{自分|じぶん}の{主張|しゅちょう}を{押|お}し{通|とお}した。
examples.english: He stuck to his position to the very end.

examples.japanese: {反対|はんたい}を{押|お}し{切|き}って{計画|けいかく}を{押|お}し{通|とお}すのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It's difficult to push a plan through against opposition.

examples.japanese: {群衆|ぐんしゅう}を{押|お}し{通|とお}す。
{人垣|ひとがき}を{押|お}し{通|とお}して{前|まえ}に{出|で}た。
examples.english: I pushed through the wall of people and got to the front.

examples.japanese: {警備|けいび}を{押|お}し{通|とお}して{会場|かいじょう}に{入|はい}ろうとした。
examples.english: He tried to force his way past security and into the venue.

notes:
A compound godan verb ({押|お}す + {通|とお}す) meaning to push something all the way through. The figurative sense of persisting stubbornly is more common than the physical sense.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {意見|いけん}を{押|お}し{通|とお}す: to push through one's opinion
- {主張|しゅちょう}を{押|お}し{通|とお}す: to insist on one's claim
- {我|わ}を{押|お}し{通|とお}す: to insist on having one's way
- {無理|むり}を{押|お}し{通|とお}す: to force something unreasonable through

USAGE:
Often carries a negative nuance of stubbornness or forceful behavior, though it can also convey admirable determination depending on context.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {押|お}し{切|き}る: to override, to push past — emphasizes overcoming resistance at a specific point
- {貫|つらぬ}く: to carry through, to stick to — more literary; emphasizes unwavering commitment to principles
- {通|とお}す: to let through, to carry through — broader meaning; {押|お}し{通|とお}す adds the forceful element
